extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers (investigators, study section members, and institutional research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria used to review NIH research project grant applications (e.g., R01, R03, R21, K awards), including scoring rules, review criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment), and Rigor & Reproducibility expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness check and error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted to NIH, your application is checked for completeness. Errors related to application processing are flagged by Grants.gov and errors related to the application requirements are detected by the eRA system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any errors identified at this stage must be addressed and the application resubmitted. It is important to submit early so that errors can be corrected prior to the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with NIH mission, overlap, and FOA/formatting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are manually checked by NIH staff for fit with the NIH mission, overlap with other applications you may have under review, and compliance with the FOA instructions and NIH formatting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with all NIH guidelines could result in the withdrawal/rejection of your application by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to appropriate study section
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to a Scientific Review Group (SRG) or study section by the Division of Receipt and Referral (DRR). Applicants can indicate preferred study section and funding institute via the PHS Assignment Request Form (ARF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important to identify a study section that is appropriate for the review of your proposal; CSR also provides an Assisted Referral Tool that matches title/abstract/aims to appropriate study sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-level peer review structure
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH utilizes a two-level peer review process: first-level review managed by CSR or an Institute/Center carried out by a study section; second-level review by each NIH Institute/Center Advisory Council/Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Council considers research priorities of the IC, input from program staff, first-level overall impact scores, percentile scores (if applicable), and summary statements before making funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system (9-point rating scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH grant application scoring system uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) in whole numbers (no decimals) for Overall Impact and Criterion (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A score of 5 is considered an average score. Reviewers submit preliminary scores prior to the meeting and final scores after discussion. The final overall impact score is calculated by multiplying the mean of the final impact scores by 10 and reported on the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and meaning of percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile is the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from a given study section over the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles (when applicable) are used by Advisory Councils and ICs in making funding recommendations alongside overall impact scores and summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council funding considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advisory Board/Council considers the research priorities of the given IC and input from relevant program staff as well as the overall impact scores awarded during the first level of peer review, the percentile scores (if applicable), and the summary statements before making funding recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications endorsed by the study section, program staff, and the Advisory Council are recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the Directors of the respective NIH ICs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an Overall Impact score that reflects their evaluation of the potential for the project to impact the relevant research field, as determined by their assessments of the scored review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact is informed by the five scored criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) and is submitted as an integer 1–9 (mean multiplied by 10 for reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: Reviewers evaluate whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific premise (strengths/weaknesses of prior research cited) is evaluated as part of the Significance criterion for research grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s): Reviewers assess whether the investigators are well qualified to conduct the proposed work and have the appropriate experience and track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes team expertise, leadership, and whether the investigative team is suited to complete the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: Reviewers assess whether the application employs novel concepts, approaches, or methods and whether it challenges current paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the project shifts existing research or clinical practice paradigms, or applies novel approaches or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach: Reviewers evaluate the rigor and feasibility of the experimental design, methods, analyses, and the overall strategy to accomplish the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific rigor (experimental design, controls, bias reduction strategies, power analyses, statistical methods) and plans to address relevant biological variables are assessed as part of the Approach criterion and the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment: Reviewers assess whether the institutional support, equipment, and other resources are adequate to ensure the project’s success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes institutional setting contributions and any special facilities or collaborative arrangements that strengthen the probability of project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Premise (Rigor & Reproducibility component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Premise: The research used to form the basis for the proposed research questions; applicants must describe general strengths and weaknesses of the prior research being cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate scientific premise as part of the Significance criterion and assess whether the applicant has discussed strengths/weaknesses of foundational data and how proposed research will address identified weaknesses or gaps. Attention should include rigor of prior experimental designs, relevant biological variables, and authentication of key resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Rigor (Rigor & Reproducibility component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Rigor: Strict application of the scientific method to ensure robust and unbiased experimental design, methodology, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of results; includes transparent reporting of experimental details for reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess scientific rigor as part of the Approach criterion and the overall impact score, evaluating experimental design, description of controls, plans to reduce bias (blinding, randomization, inclusion/exclusion criteria), power analyses, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of relevant biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of Relevant Biological Variables: Applicants must address variables such as sex, age, weight, and underlying health conditions when they affect outcomes; sex is highlighted as frequently ignored in animal study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess plans to address relevant biological variables as part of the Approach criterion and overall impact. If only one sex is proposed, reviewers will assess the applicant's justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of key resources (e.g., cell lines, special chemicals, antibodies, transgenic animals, other biologics): applicants must provide plans for authentication because these resources may vary over time and across labs and can influence research data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers discuss adequacy of the authentication plan after scoring; comments on authentication should not affect scores. However, an inadequate or missing authentication plan will be reflected in the written critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with peer review policies and ethical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must comply with peer review regulations and policies, including conflict of interest, rigor & reproducibility, human subjects protections, vertebrate animal protections, and scoring procedures for research applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER provides information on peer review compliance and oversight; reviewers and applicants should consult NIH Grants Policy Statement and Peer Review Policies and Practices for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility for Early Career Reviewer (ECR) participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility criteria for NIH Early Career Reviewer program: individuals must have 2 years of experience in a full-time faculty or research position, show evidence of an active independent program of research, have at least two recent senior-authored research publications, and may not have served on a CSR study section (mail reviews not counted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current funding is not required. NIH specifically seeks participation of early career reviewers through this program; serving as a reviewer may allow certain submission incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting and critique preparation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are provided resources on pre-meeting logistics, preparing for review, guidance on scoring and writing critiques, and updates to peer review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR and OER provide downloadable reviewer guidelines and fillable critique templates for all funding mechanisms; reviewers should follow those templates and scoring guidance when preparing written critiques.
